## A Change of Labels Must Preserve the Measured Quantity

For a smooth invertible local coordinate change $x=x(z)$ with $T=D_zx$, perturbations obey $\delta x=T\delta z$. A specified quadratic form transforms as $M_z=T^\top M_xT$, preserving $\delta x^\top M_x\delta x$. This statement applies between charts of the same dimension. A task map or an embedding in a higher-dimensional ambient space is not generally an invertible change of coordinates.

The differential flow transports tangent vectors between their base points. Coordinate expressions for its derivative are valid; under changing charts, the dynamics and the metric derivative must transform together [@forni2014contraction].

## Task Pullback and Unmeasured Directions

For $y=h(x)$, $J=Dh\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}$ and $W\succ0$, the task penalty is

$$
M_{\rm task}=J^\top WJ.
$$

It is positive definite exactly when $J$ has full column rank. When $p<n$, that is impossible. A position-only task also misses velocity directions in a mechanical state. This rank deficiency can express a legitimate output objective; it cannot certify full-state contraction by itself.

A completion $M=M_{\rm task}+\varepsilon M_0$, with $\varepsilon>0$ and a declared positive background metric $M_0$, changes the objective by penalizing other directions. Specify units and scaling. Adding an identity in every chart does not preserve one physical metric: for $J=(1,0)$, $\varepsilon=0.1$, $M_0=I$, $T=\operatorname{diag}(2,3)$, transformation gives $\operatorname{diag}(4.4,0.9)$, whereas adding $0.1I$ after transforming $J$ gives $\operatorname{diag}(4.1,0.1)$.

## A Hessian Is Not Automatically a Metric

Under a nonlinear coordinate change,

$$
D_z^2V=T^\top D_x^2V\,T+\sum_i(D_xV)_iD_z^2x_i.
$$

For $V(x)=x^2/2$ and $x=\log z$, the coordinate Hessian is $(1-\log z)/z^2$. At $z=e^2$ it is negative, while the pullback of the positive form $1$ is $1/z^2>0$. The extra term vanishes at stationary points. A covariant Hessian requires a chosen connection and is still not guaranteed positive. Transforming a Riccati quadratic form and recomputing a nonlinear value Hessian are therefore different operations.
